prototypeScope: V1.25 delta package, the two-half ankle with a round sleeve bore: one Orange plate with the outer and inner halves of both ankles. V1.22 and V1.24 are printed (Shawn 2026-10-20); the V1.22 black sleeves and yellow slip-fit feet stay.
knownFitBoundary: The two halves meet 0.2 mm apart at the cut; the foot socket (0.15-0.19 mm play to the stock envelope) and the toe M2 x 6 hold them. The sleeve keeps about 0.4 mm of diametral running clearance once the support is out of the bore and the bore is scraped smooth. Printed sizes are not measured; if the foot is tight on the two halves, sand the socket walls of the foot, never force it. Not fitted yet.
processOverrideReason: Stock profile (brims per object by the pipeline R1 rule or the manifest objectSettings).

parts.poseOrigin: local +x down (gusset end face on the bed): The gusset end face on the bed, as the V1.22 base and the 10/07 candidate: the motor mating face, the four output seats and the cut face stand vertical. Bambu: every MUST face clean.

parts.changeReason: Replaces the printed community-66.stl (stock object 20, the left one-piece ankle bracket) together with ankle_inner_left; it also replaces the V1.22 ankle base. Shawn 2026-10-20: the V1.22 base and side look fragile, need careful support removal, and their two pairs of screw posts catch the servo wire. This is the stock bracket for local z < -16.1 (the cut at the toe screw axis, set back 0.1 mm): the plate on the servo horn with the four M2 x 4 seats as before and half of the foot block. The link-servo-sleeve package sits straight down into it (halves-check.json packageLiftOutOfOuterClearMm 30). The V1.22 slip-fit foot seats on both halves exactly as on the stock bracket (footSeat play, drop contact) and holds them together.
parts.objectSettingsReason: Every half stands 36.5 mm tall on a 41 mm2 end face; one V1.24 outer half in this pose came off the bed mid-print with the R1 4 mm brim (2026-10-20), and Bambu advises a wider brim for a taller part on a smaller footprint (orientation-study/PRINT-ORIENTATION-PRACTICE.md R1). 8 mm outer brim, 0.1 mm gap.
parts.brimInsideHullAllowanceReason: The gusset end face on the bed carries the real 12 x 1.1 mm recess of the stock bracket (community-66/64 notch beside the gusset hole); the outer half keeps part of it. Bambu Studio loops the 4 mm outer brim into it: 2.4 mm2 inside the convex outline on both outer halves, a strip bonded on three sides, cut it out with a blade. Orca puts support feet there instead. Same notch as the V1.22 bases (13.3 mm2 there). Not an opening filled with brim.

parts.sourceFrame: ankle-halves-20261020 local frame of the left ankle inner half (mm; motor shaft = local z, up = local y)
parts.poseOrigin: local +x down (toe end on the bed, shaft flat, round bore): Shawn 2026-10-20 on the printed V1.24 teardrop: the d15 pocket and the d14 lip bore stay round and support may stand in the hole. The half stands on its toe end (the stock face that carries the cut gusset; the same pose as the outer half), so the shaft lies flat and the bore's top in print is its heel side on the robot. The support inside the bore touches that heel-side band; the bore's lower side, which carries the robot's weight, prints as a vertical wall with no support on it.

parts.changeReason: New part, with ankle_outer_left replacing the printed community-66.stl (stock object 20); it also replaces the V1.22 ankle side. The stock bracket for local z > -15.9: the plate whose pocket runs on the 10.4 mm V1.22 sleeve, with its sleeve lip raised from 0.25-0.5 mm to 1.2 mm, the d15 pocket and d14 lip bore round as on the stock bracket (V1.24 had a 45 deg teardrop roof; Shawn 2026-10-20 wants the bore round with support in it), and the other half of the foot block. No screw, post or tab of its own.
